item.title: A bollard gone, 21st September
item.description:
The pavement bollard beside the speed cushions has been completely knocked down/sheared off, leaving only the base in the pavement. This bollard is particularly important because vehicles regularly mount the pavement at this location to avoid driving over the speed cushions. Without the bollard, vehicles can drive along the pavement, creating a serious risk to pedestrians, including children and vulnerable people. The remaining bollard base may also itself present a trip hazard. Please could the Council inspect this location and replace the bollard as soon as possible.

item.title: Cambridge Gardens, 21st September
item.description:
Every Saturday, the London Car Boot Sale - a privately operated commercial event - attracts large numbers of unauthorised street traders who set up outside the designated site and sell stolen goods along the surrounding streets and pavements. While the organisers benefit commercially from the event, the consequences outside the gates are left for local residents, businesses and the Council to deal with: aggressive behaviour, obstructed pavements, illegal trading and significant amounts of rubbish left behind. These problems are neither new nor occasional; concerns are well documented and have been reported for years and the disruption now occurs predictably every Saturday. Given the longstanding and recurring nature of the problem, there is a strong case for coordinated action across the relevant Council and enforcement teams rather than continuing to treat each Saturday as an isolated incident. This is precisely the kind of recurring local problem where government should be visible and effective. The answer cannot simply be that there are insufficient resources and therefore the community must learn to live with it. What is needed is ownership of the problem, clarity over which authorities and enforcement powers apply, and a coordinated plan to resolve it.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Cambridge Gardens, London
